subject: Uptime baseline granularity and monthly credit escrow request
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acme.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: David Liu <david.liu@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 01 Nov 2025 10:13:00 -0700
Subject: Initial SLA ask — uptime baseline and monthly credit cap

Hi Stephanie / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement asked me to capture the ask in writing so we can take a clean redline to legal. Two items to confirm:

1) Uptime baseline: Acme typically requires a 99.95% monthly availability commitment for production endpoints.
2) Monthly service credit: we prefer a meaningful remedy but need a cap that limits our vendor exposure to 30% of the monthly bill. We can be flexible on tiers (e.g., 99.95 -> 5% credit, 99.5 -> 15%, <99% -> 30%).

Also calling out onboarding months: our finance team asks that the first two months after go-live be eligible for reduced caps while usage ramps — effectively a temporary credit floor modification. Can you confirm if Redwood can entertain a one-time onboarding carveout?

I've attached our standard scoring sheet and a sample credit table for reference. Please let me know the earliest you can provide a proposed alternate that we can send to legal.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp
Attachment: SLA_credit_calculation.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acme.com>, David Liu <david.liu@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Nov 2025 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial SLA ask — uptime baseline and monthly credit cap

Maya — thanks for the clear note and the spreadsheet. Appreciate the example tiers; that helps a lot. A few points from our side:

- Baseline: our standard hosted SLA template typically uses a 99.9% monthly availability commitment for shared-hosted endpoints. We can support 99.95% for dedicated or reserved capacity configurations (and for larger committed deals).

- Credits: we propose a tiered credit approach that is predictable and caps at 20% of the monthly invoice (we've found this balances incentives without creating outsized financial transfer risk for early-stage accounts). Example proposed tiers (for discussion):
  • >=99.9% — 0%
  • 99.5%–99.9% — 7%
  • 99.0%–99.5% — 15%
  • <99.0% — 20% cap

- Onboarding carveout: we can offer a time-limited onboarding modification for the first 60 days post-prod where the cap increases to 30% if you purchase Reserved Capacity for the pilot or sign a 12-month commitment. If it's a pure hosted month-to-month pilot, we can offer a single-month exception at our discretion.

I've attached a redline of our SLA draft with these numbers called out (Redwood_SLA_Draft_Acme_v3.pdf). Can you confirm whether Acme expects the 99.95% requirement to apply to hosted endpoints or only to dedicated pools? That will determine internal approvals we need.

If you like, I can loop Karthik (pricing) and Laura (legal approvals) for a quick call tomorrow to finalize the numbers before sending to your legal team.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Draft_Acme_v3.pdf (PDF)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Internal — Acme SLA: 99.95 ask and onboarding carveout (need signoff)

Team — quick note with proposed positions before I send our final counter to Acme: 

Summary of external ask:
- Acme wants 99.95% monthly for production (they did not specify Dedicated vs Hosted).
- Credit cap requested: 30% monthly.
- They want the first two months onboarding carveout with higher caps.

Our recommended compromise:
- Offer 99.95% for Dedicated only, 99.9% for Hosted.
- Use the tiered credit schedule below with a 20% cap standard; 30% cap only if customer commits to 12 months reserved capacity or we pre-approve a two-month ramp exception on a case-by-case basis.
  • >=99.9 — 0%
  • 99.5–99.9 — 7%
  • 99.0–99.5 — 15%
  • <99.0 — 20% cap

Risk/notes:
- Legal will likely push back on the 30% onboarding cap. If Acme insists, we should require either an advance commitment or an early-termination fee to offset risk.
- Finance: if we make an exception for onboarding, we should limit the total liability over the first quarter (e.g., $X or Y% whichever lower) to avoid open-ended exposure. Karthik — can you quickly run a worst-case cost estimate for a $100k/month consumption profile under a 30% cap?

I'll draft the reply and send to Acme after you both confirm.

Thanks,
Stephanie
From: David Liu <david.liu@acme.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial SLA ask — uptime baseline and monthly credit cap

Stephanie — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the clear options. A few clarifications from procurement and finance after reviewing your redline:

1) Hosted vs Dedicated: Acme's initial deployment will be hosted (no reserved capacity commitment for the first 3 months). That means we'd need the higher 99.95% baseline to apply to hosted endpoints for this contract, otherwise the business can't accept risk.

2) Credit cap: we can accept tiered credits, but the cap needs to be 30% for the first 90 days if we do not sign a 12-month commitment. After 90 days, if both parties are satisfied, reduce cap to 20%.

3) Calculation example: can Redwood provide a worked example of the credit calculation for a $250k monthly bill at 99.2% availability (showing the dollar credit and cap effect)? That will speed our legal review.

If you can update the draft PDF and share a simple worked example spreadsheet, we can get the DocuSign routing started. We also opened a HubSpot deal (link below).

Regards,
David Liu
Director, Cloud Ops — Acme Corp
